source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's DFW1 campus in Carrollton, Texas publishes 45 MW of IT capacity across 600,000 square feet of technical space, and that figure is the operator's own.

The number matters because it is one of the few in Texas that can be counted at all. Texas holds 137 mapped facilities, but only 19 publish a megawatt figure, and those 19 total 475.41 MW. DFW1's 45 MW ranks third among them. The gap between 137 mapped and 19 publishing is the real story: most of the state's capacity is invisible to any count we can make, and this campus is one of the few that lets itself be counted.

The certifications, read narrowly, qualify the campus to host payment card data, protected health data, federal information systems, and audited financial controls. TIA-942 speaks to the physical topology of the facility itself. None of them name a customer, and the spec page publishes no address, postal code, or tenant list, so nothing here says who runs inside it.

What the data does not give is a rack count, a rack density, or a cooling method. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 45 MW of IT load is roughly 1,125 racks, but that is an assumption about rack power, not a claim by CyrusOne. At 130 kW per rack, a plausible figure for a dense liquid-cooled deployment, the same 45 MW would be about 346 racks. The accelerator count is not derivable from this page at all.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
